source.text: שִׁ֥יר הַֽמַּֽעֲל֗וֹת לִשְׁלֹ֫מֹ֥האִם־יְהוָ֤ה׀לֹא־יִבְנֶ֬ה בַ֗יִת שָׁ֤וְא׀עָמְל֣וּ בוֹנָ֣יו בּ֑וֹ אִם־יְהוָ֥ה לֹֽא־יִשְׁמָר־עִ֝֗יר שָׁ֤וְא׀שָׁקַ֬ד שׁוֹמֵֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: The song of the ascents, of Solomon. If YHWH not will build a house, in vain have toiled its builders on it; if YHWH not will keep a city, in vain has kept awake [the] watchman.

en.L: A song of ascents. Of Solomon. If {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} does not build a house, in vain its builders have toiled on it; if {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} does not keep a city, in vain the watchman has kept awake.
en.B: A song of ascents. Of Solomon. If {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} does not build the house, the work of its builders comes to nothing. If {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} does not guard the city, the watchman's sleepless night is wasted.
en.R: A song for the journey up to Jerusalem. By Solomon. If {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is not the one building a house, the builders are wasting their work. If {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is not guarding a city, the guards are wasting their time staying awake.

fr.L: Cantique des montées. De Salomon. Si {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ne bâtit pas la maison, c’est en vain que ses bâtisseurs y ont peiné ; si {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ne garde pas la ville, c’est en vain que le veilleur a veillé.
fr.B: Cantique des montées. De Salomon. Si {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ne bâtit pas la maison, le travail des bâtisseurs ne sert à rien. Si {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ne garde pas la ville, le veilleur passe sa nuit sans dormir pour rien.
fr.R: Chant pour la montée vers Jérusalem. De Salomon. Si ce n’est pas {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} qui construit une maison, les ouvriers perdent leur peine. Si ce n’est pas {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} qui garde une ville, les gardes restent éveillés pour rien.

sw.L: Wimbo wa kupanda. Wa Sulemani. Kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} hajengi nyumba, wajenzi wake wamejitaabisha bure juu yake; kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} haulindi mji, mlinzi amekesha bure.
sw.B: Wimbo wa kupanda. Wa Sulemani. Ikiwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} si {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} anayejenga nyumba, kazi ya wajenzi wake inakuwa bure. Ikiwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} haulindi mji, kukesha kwa mlinzi usiku kucha ni bure.
sw.R: Wimbo wa safari ya kupanda kwenda Yerusalemu. Wa Sulemani. Kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} si {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} anayejenga nyumba, wajenzi wanapoteza kazi yao. Kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} si {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} anayeulinda mji, walinzi wanapoteza muda wao kukaa macho.

es.L: Cántico de las subidas. De Salomón. Si {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} no edifica una casa, en vano se han fatigado en ella sus constructores; si {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} no guarda una ciudad, en vano ha velado el centinela.
es.B: Cántico de las subidas. De Salomón. Si {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} no construye la casa, el trabajo de los constructores no sirve de nada. Si {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} no cuida la ciudad, la noche en vela del centinela se pierde.
es.R: Canto para el viaje de subida a Jerusalén. De Salomón. Si no es {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} quien construye una casa, los constructores están desperdiciando su trabajo. Si no es {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} quien cuida una ciudad, los guardias pierden el tiempo quedándose despiertos.

vi.L: Bài ca cho những lần đi lên. Của Sa-lô-môn. Nếu {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} không xây nhà, thì những người xây nhà đã nhọc công trên đó cách vô ích; nếu {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} không canh giữ thành, thì người canh gác đã thức canh cách vô ích.
vi.B: Bài ca đi lên. Của Sa-lô-môn. Nếu {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} không xây nhà, công lao của người thợ xây chỉ là uổng phí. Nếu {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} không canh giữ thành, đêm không ngủ của người lính canh cũng thành vô ích.
vi.R: Bài ca cho cuộc hành trình lên Giê-ru-sa-lem. Của Sa-lô-môn. Nếu {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} không phải là Đấng xây nhà, thì những người thợ xây chỉ phí công. Nếu {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} không canh giữ thành, thì những người lính canh thức canh cũng chỉ phí thời giờ.

ko.L: 올라감을 위한 노래. 솔로몬의 [노래]. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 집을 세우지 않으시면, 그 집을 세우는 자들이 거기서 수고한 것이 헛되다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 성을 지키지 않으시면, 파수꾼이 깨어 있었던 것이 헛되다.
ko.B: 올라가며 부르는 노래. 솔로몬의 노래. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 집을 세우지 않으시면 집 짓는 사람들의 수고가 다 쓸데없다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 성을 지키지 않으시면 파수꾼이 잠 못 들고 지새운 밤도 헛일이다.
ko.R: 예루살렘으로 올라가며 부르는 노래. 솔로몬의 노래. 집을 짓는 분이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 아니시면, 일꾼들은 헛수고를 하는 것이다. 성을 지키는 분이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 아니시면, 경비병들이 잠을 안 자고 지키는 것도 헛일이다.

decisions.choice: The title shares verse 1
decisions.reason: As in 120:1, the short title and the first line are counted together as verse 1, so the verse numbers are the same as in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: a song of ascents: probably a pilgrim song
decisions.reason: As in 120:1: one of the fifteen songs probably sung by pilgrims going up to Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: of Solomon: linked with Solomon
decisions.reason: This is one of two psalms linked with Solomon (with Psalm 72). Solomon built the LORD's house (1 Kings 6), and "his beloved" in verse 2 (yedid) echoes his other name, Jedidiah, "beloved of the LORD" (2 Samuel 12:25). Some ancient copies of the title lack the name.

decisions.choice: a house: a building, and a household
decisions.reason: "Build a house" can mean to put up a building or to found a family (Ruth 4:11; 2 Samuel 7:27). The second half of the psalm (verses 3-5) turns to children, so both senses are probably in view; the temple may be heard too.

decisions.choice: in vain: for nothing
decisions.reason: The word (shav') means emptiness, what has no result. It comes three times in verses 1-2.

decisions.choice: A song for the journey up to Jerusalem
decisions.reason: As in 120:1.

decisions.choice: "솔로몬의 [노래]" (L), "솔로몬의 노래" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As "다윗의 노래" in this block: the Hebrew "of Solomon" may name the author or the one the song concerns (meaning decision), and "의" keeps that open.

source.text: שָׁ֤וְא לָכֶ֨ם׀מַשְׁכִּ֪ימֵי ק֡וּם מְאַֽחֲרֵי־שֶׁ֗בֶת אֹ֭כְלֵי לֶ֣חֶם הָעֲצָבִ֑ים כֵּ֤ן יִתֵּ֖ן לִֽידִיד֣וֹ שֵׁנָֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: In vain [it is] for you, [who] rise early to rise, [who] delay to sit, [who] eat the bread of the toils; so he gives to his beloved sleep.

en.L: [It is] in vain for you who rise early, who stay up late, who eat the bread of toils; so {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gives to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} beloved sleep.
en.B: It does you no good to get up early and stay up late, eating food earned by anxious work; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gives sleep to the one {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} loves.
en.R: It is no use getting up early and going to bed late, working so hard just to have food to eat. God gives sleep to the people {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} loves.

fr.L: [C’est] en vain pour vous qui vous levez tôt, qui tardez à vous asseoir, qui mangez le pain des peines ; ainsi {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} donne à {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} bien-aimé le sommeil.
fr.B: Inutile de vous lever tôt et de vous coucher tard, de manger un pain gagné dans l’angoisse : {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} donne le sommeil à celui qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} aime.
fr.R: Ça ne sert à rien de se lever tôt et de se coucher tard, de travailler si dur juste pour avoir à manger. Dieu donne le sommeil aux gens qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} aime.

sw.L: [Ni] bure kwenu ninyi mnaoamka mapema, mnaochelewa kukaa, mnaokula mkate wa taabu; hivyo humpa mpendwa {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} usingizi.
sw.B: Haiwafaidii kitu kuamka mapema na kuchelewa kulala, mkila chakula kilichopatikana kwa kazi ya wasiwasi; {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} humpa usingizi yule ampendaye.
sw.R: Hakuna faida kuamka mapema na kuchelewa kwenda kulala, mkifanya kazi ngumu ili tu kupata chakula. Mungu huwapa usingizi watu anaowapenda.

es.L: En vano [es] para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} madrugar, acostarse tarde, comer el pan de los trabajos penosos; así da {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} amado el sueño.
es.B: De nada {{plural_you:les|os}} sirve levantarse temprano y acostarse tarde, comiendo el pan ganado con trabajo y angustia; {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} da el sueño al que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} ama.
es.R: No sirve de nada levantarse temprano e irse a dormir tarde, trabajando tanto solo para tener algo que comer. Dios da el sueño a la gente que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} ama.

vi.L: [Thật là] vô ích cho các người, những người dậy sớm, thức khuya, ăn bánh của sự lao nhọc; {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ban giấc ngủ cho người yêu dấu của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cũng như vậy.
vi.B: Các người dậy sớm thức khuya, ăn miếng bánh kiếm được bằng lao nhọc lo âu, cũng chẳng ích gì; {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ban giấc ngủ cho người {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} yêu thương.
vi.R: Dậy sớm và đi ngủ khuya, làm việc vất vả chỉ để có miếng ăn, thật chẳng ích gì. Đức Chúa Trời ban giấc ngủ cho những người {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} yêu thương.

ko.L: 너희가 일찍 일어나고 늦게 앉으며 고된 수고의 빵을 먹는 것이 헛되다. 이처럼 그분께서는 그분이 사랑하시는 자에게 잠을 주신다.
ko.B: 일찍 일어나고 늦게까지 자지 않으며 애태우며 일해서 얻은 음식을 먹어도 너희에게 아무 소용이 없다. 그분께서는 그분이 사랑하시는 사람에게 잠을 주신다.
ko.R: 일찍 일어나고 늦게 잠자리에 들면서, 먹고살려고 그렇게 힘들게 일해도 소용없다. 하나님께서는 그분이 사랑하시는 사람들에게 잠을 주신다.

decisions.choice: gives sleep to his beloved
alternatives: gives to his beloved while they sleep
decisions.reason: "Sleep" may be what God gives (rest, instead of anxious nights), or it may describe when he gives: he provides for the one he loves even while that person sleeps. Both fit the contrast with anxious toil.

decisions.choice: so: in this way, even so
decisions.reason: The word (ken) usually means "so" or "thus". Here it marks the contrast: the anxious work for food, and in this way God gives sleep.

decisions.choice: the bread of toils: food won by painful work
decisions.reason: The word for toil ('itstsavim) is related to the painful labor of Genesis 3:17: "in toil you will eat".

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who gives.

decisions.choice: "vous" for the plural "you" of the Hebrew
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "for you" is plural, addressed to all who toil; French uses "vous". Readable turns it into a general statement with infinitives, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: plural_you on "ustedes" (L) and "les" (B)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "for you" is plural, spoken to all who wear themselves out; Spanish marks it with the plural_you setting. Readable, like the English Readable, says it without addressing anyone.

decisions.choice: "các người" for "you" spoken to the hearers
decisions.reason: The singer speaks to all who work early and late, not to an enemy, so the plain "các người" fits better than the stern "các ngươi"; Readable turns it into a general statement.

decisions.choice: "빵" for the Hebrew "bread"
decisions.reason: As the style guide ("빵", never "떡"); Balanced and Readable say food in general, as the English does.

source.text: הִנֵּ֤ה נַחֲלַ֣ת יְהוָ֣ה בָּנִ֑ים שָׂ֝כָ֗ר פְּרִ֣י הַבָּֽטֶן׃

records.literal_gloss: Look, a heritage of YHWH [are] sons, a reward [is] the fruit of the womb.

en.L: Look, a heritage from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [are] {{gender:children|sons}}; a reward [is] the fruit of the womb.
en.B: {{gender:Children|Sons}} are a gift handed down from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; the fruit of the womb is a reward.
en.R: {{gender:Children|Sons}} are a gift from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. When a baby is born, it is a reward from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

fr.L: Voici, un héritage {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, [ce sont] les {{gender:enfants|fils}} ; une récompense, [c’est] le fruit du ventre.
fr.B: Les {{gender:enfants|fils}} sont un héritage donné par {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ; le fruit du ventre est une récompense.
fr.R: Les {{gender:enfants|fils}} sont un cadeau {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. Quand un bébé naît, c’est une récompense qui vient de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.

sw.L: Tazama, urithi kutoka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} [ni] watoto; tuzo [ni] uzao wa tumbo.
sw.B: Watoto ni zawadi ya urithi itokayo kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}; uzao wa tumbo ni tuzo.
sw.R: Watoto ni zawadi kutoka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Mtoto anapozaliwa, ni tuzo kutoka {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}.

es.L: Mira, herencia {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} [son] los hijos; una recompensa [es] el fruto del vientre.
es.B: Los hijos son un regalo que se recibe {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}; el fruto del vientre es una recompensa.
es.R: Los hijos son un regalo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. Cuando nace un bebé, es una recompensa que viene de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.

vi.L: Này, {{gender:con cái|con trai}} [là] cơ nghiệp đến từ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}; bông trái của lòng mẹ [là] phần thưởng.
vi.B: {{gender:Con cái|Con trai}} là món quà {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ban để truyền lại; bông trái của lòng mẹ là phần thưởng.
vi.R: {{gender:Con cái|Con trai}} là món quà {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ban cho. Khi một em bé ra đời, đó là phần thưởng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ban.

ko.L: 보아라, {{gender:자녀들|아들들}}은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 주신 유산이고, 태의 열매는 상급이다.
ko.B: {{gender:자녀들|아들들}}은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 물려주신 선물이고, 태에서 난 열매는 상급이다.
ko.R: {{gender:자녀들|아들들}}은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 주신 선물이다. 아기가 태어나는 것은 그분께서 주시는 상이다.

decisions.choice: heritage: a gift that is passed down
decisions.reason: The word (nachalah) is the share of land each family received from the LORD and passed on. Children, like the land, are the LORD's gift.

decisions.choice: sons: children
decisions.reason: The word (banim) is used of sons and of children in general. "The fruit of the womb" includes daughters; verses 4-5 picture grown sons who defend the family.

decisions.choice: children
decisions.reason: The default says "children" (m2); the gender setting gives "sons".

decisions.choice: from him
decisions.reason: Readable repeats who gives the reward, which the parallel line implies.

decisions.choice: "enfants" by default, "fils" as the gender alternative, for banim
decisions.reason: Banim here means children, as the meaning decision says; French puts the setting on the noun, with "enfants" by default and the traditional "fils" as the alternative.

decisions.choice: "watoto" (children) with no gender setting
alternatives: "wana wa kiume" (sons) as a traditional alternative
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "sons" here means children (see the meaning decision). Swahili says "watoto"; "wana wa kiume" would mean boys only and change the sense, so there is no setting, unlike the English.

decisions.choice: hijos, with no gender setting
decisions.reason: The English has a setting for "children" or "sons". Spanish "hijos" already means children of both sexes as well as sons, so it stays plain here and in verse 4.

decisions.choice: "con cái" by default, with "con trai" (sons) as the gender alternative
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is "sons" but means children (see the meaning decision); Vietnamese has both words, as the English has "children" and "sons", so the setting can offer the traditional form.

decisions.choice: {{gender:자녀들|아들들}} in verses 3-4, both forms plural so one particle fits
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word means sons but here stands for children (meaning decision); Korean has both wordings, as the English does. Both end in "들", so "은" and "이" fit either.

records.literal_gloss: Like arrows in [the] hand of a warrior, so [are] the sons of the youth.

en.L: Like arrows in the hand of a warrior, so [are] the {{gender:children|sons}} of [one's] youth.
en.B: {{gender:Children|Sons}} born to the young are like arrows in a fighter's hand.
en.R: {{gender:Children|Sons}} born when their parents are young are like arrows in a soldier's hand. They help to protect the family.

fr.L: Comme des flèches dans la main d’un guerrier, ainsi [sont] les {{gender:enfants|fils}} de la jeunesse.
fr.B: Les {{gender:enfants|fils}} qu’on a dans sa jeunesse sont comme des flèches dans la main d’un combattant.
fr.R: Les {{gender:enfants|fils}} nés quand les parents sont jeunes sont comme des flèches dans la main d’un soldat. Ils aident à protéger la famille.

sw.L: Kama mishale mkononi mwa shujaa, ndivyo [walivyo] watoto wa ujanani.
sw.B: Watoto wanaozaliwa na wazazi vijana ni kama mishale mkononi mwa mpiganaji.
sw.R: Watoto wanaozaliwa wazazi wao wakiwa bado vijana ni kama mishale mkononi mwa askari. Wanasaidia kuilinda familia.

es.L: Como flechas en la mano de un guerrero, así [son] los hijos de la juventud.
es.B: Los hijos que se tienen de joven son como flechas en la mano de un guerrero.
es.R: Los hijos que nacen cuando sus padres son jóvenes son como flechas en la mano de un soldado. Ayudan a proteger a la familia.

vi.L: Như những mũi tên trong tay dũng sĩ, {{gender:con cái|con trai}} của tuổi xuân [cũng] vậy.
vi.B: {{gender:Con cái|Con trai}} sinh ra lúc còn trẻ giống như những mũi tên trong tay người chiến binh.
vi.R: {{gender:Con cái|Con trai}} sinh ra khi cha mẹ còn trẻ giống như những mũi tên trong tay người lính. Chúng giúp bảo vệ gia đình.

ko.L: 용사의 손에 있는 화살들 같으니, 젊은 시절의 {{gender:자녀들|아들들}}이 그러하다.
ko.B: 젊어서 낳은 {{gender:자녀들|아들들}}은 용사의 손에 들린 화살과 같다.
ko.R: 부모가 젊을 때 낳은 {{gender:자녀들|아들들}}은 군인의 손에 들린 화살과 같다. 그들은 가족을 지키는 데 힘이 된다.

decisions.choice: the sons of youth: children born early in life
decisions.reason: Children born while their father is young are grown and strong while he still needs them, able to stand with him and defend the family.

decisions.choice: arrows in a warrior's hand: strength and defense
decisions.reason: Arrows are a warrior's means of defense and of reaching an enemy at a distance. The picture continues with the quiver in verse 5.

decisions.choice: children
decisions.reason: As in verse 3.

decisions.choice: They help to protect the family
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture means (m1, m2).

source.text: אַשְׁרֵ֤י הַגֶּ֗בֶר אֲשֶׁ֤ר מִלֵּ֥א אֶת־אַשְׁפָּת֗וֹ מֵ֫הֶ֥ם לֹֽא־יֵבֹ֑שׁוּ כִּֽי־יְדַבְּר֖וּ אֶת־אוֹיְבִ֣ים בַּשָּֽׁעַר׃

records.literal_gloss: How blessed [is] the man who has filled his quiver with them; not they will be ashamed when they speak with enemies in the gate.

en.L: How blessed [is] {{gender:the one|the man}} who has filled {{gender:their|his}} quiver with them! They will not be put to shame when they speak with enemies in the gate.
en.B: How blessed is {{gender:the one|the man}} who has a quiver filled with them! They will not be disgraced when they argue with enemies at the city gate.
en.R: Life is truly good for anyone whose quiver is full of such arrows! When they meet enemies in court at the city gate, they will not be put to shame.

fr.L: {{gender:Heureuse la personne|Heureux l’homme}} qui en a rempli son carquois ! Ils ne seront pas couverts de honte quand ils parleront avec des ennemis à la porte.
fr.B: {{gender:Heureuse la personne|Heureux l’homme}} qui en a rempli son carquois ! Ils ne seront pas humiliés quand ils discuteront avec des ennemis à la porte de la ville.
fr.R: La vie est vraiment belle pour celui dont le carquois est plein de ces flèches ! Quand ils rencontreront des ennemis au tribunal, à la porte de la ville, ils ne seront pas couverts de honte.

sw.L: Heri mtu ambaye amelijaza podo lake kwa hao! Hawataaibishwa watakaposema na adui langoni.
sw.B: Heri mtu aliye na podo lililojaa hao! Hawataaibika wanaposhindana na adui kwenye lango la mji.
sw.R: Maisha ni mazuri kweli kwa mtu ambaye podo lake limejaa mishale ya namna hiyo! Wanapokutana na adui mahakamani kwenye lango la mji, hawataaibika.

es.L: ¡{{gender:Dichosa la persona|Dichoso el hombre}} que ha llenado su aljaba de ellos! No serán avergonzados cuando hablen con los enemigos en la puerta.
es.B: ¡Qué {{gender:dichosa es la persona|dichoso es el hombre}} que tiene la aljaba llena de ellos! No quedarán en vergüenza cuando discutan con los enemigos en la puerta de la ciudad.
es.R: ¡Qué buena es la vida de quien tiene la aljaba llena de esas flechas! Cuando se encuentren con sus enemigos en el tribunal, a la puerta de la ciudad, no quedarán en vergüenza.

vi.L: Phước thay người đã làm đầy ống tên mình bằng chúng! Họ sẽ không bị hổ thẹn khi nói với kẻ thù tại cổng thành.
vi.B: Phước hạnh thay người có ống tên đầy những mũi tên ấy! Họ sẽ không bị hổ thẹn khi tranh luận với kẻ thù tại cổng thành.
vi.R: Thật hạnh phúc cho người nào có ống tên đầy những mũi tên như thế! Khi gặp kẻ thù trước tòa xét xử ở cổng thành, họ sẽ không bị hổ thẹn.

ko.L: 그것들로 자기 화살통을 가득 채운 사람은 얼마나 복된가! 그들이 성문에서 원수들과 말할 때 수치를 당하지 않을 것이다.
ko.B: 그런 화살로 화살통을 가득 채운 사람은 얼마나 복된가! 그들은 성문에서 원수들과 다툴 때 부끄러움을 당하지 않을 것이다.
ko.R: 그런 화살로 화살통이 가득한 사람은 참으로 행복하다! 성문에서 열리는 재판에서 원수들을 만나도 그들은 부끄러움을 당하지 않을 것이다.

decisions.choice: How blessed: how good the life of
decisions.reason: The exclamation ('ashre) of 1:1: a life that goes well.

decisions.choice: in the gate: at the city court
decisions.reason: The city gate was where the elders sat to settle disputes and where business was done (Deuteronomy 21:19; Ruth 4:1-11; Amos 5:12). A man with grown sons had support when an opponent brought a case against him.

decisions.choice: they: the father with his sons
decisions.reason: The verbs change to "they": the father and his sons together stand up to the enemy.

decisions.choice: Life is truly good for
decisions.reason: As in 1:1.

decisions.choice: the one
decisions.reason: The word (gever) is "a man", here a father; as in Psalm 1 the default makes the blessing general and the gender setting gives "the man". Readable says "anyone".

decisions.choice: "Heureux" for ʾashrei at Literal and Balanced; Readable says what it means ("La vie est vraiment belle pour")
decisions.reason: ʾAshrei is an exclamation about how good a life is, not the word for blessing by God (barukh). "Heureux" is the French word for this exclamation; the English "How blessed" says the same thing.

decisions.choice: "Heri mtu" (L, B); "Maisha ni mazuri kweli kwa mtu" (R), with no gender setting
decisions.reason: "Heri" is the Swahili word that declares someone truly happy; it is not "amebarikiwa", which would say God has blessed him. Readable spells it out as the English Readable does. "Mtu" means a man or a woman, so the English gender setting has nothing to change.

decisions.choice: Dichosa la persona / Dichoso el hombre (L, B); Qué buena es la vida de quien (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew ashre says how well a life goes. Literal and Balanced use "dichoso", agreeing with its noun inside the gender setting; Readable says the person's life is good, as the English Readable does, and as earlier Psalms do.

decisions.choice: "Phước thay người" (L), "Phước hạnh thay người" (B), "Thật hạnh phúc cho người" (R), with no gender span, as Psalm 1:1
alternatives: gender spans as in the English ("the one"/"the man")
decisions.reason: The exclamation and its wording follow the published Psalm 1:1. "người" already means anyone, man or woman, so Vietnamese has no second form for the setting to give.

decisions.choice: "얼마나 복된가" (L, B), "참으로 행복하다" (R) for ashrei, as the published Psalm 1:1; "사람" with no gender span
decisions.reason: Psalm 1:1 fixes this wording for the Psalter. "사람" is the ordinary word for a person of either sex, so Korean has no second wording for the English "the one|the man" span (as Psalm 1:1); the same holds in 128:4.
